review_notes: I read the whole file and its clients: MultivariatePolynomialsTests/BlockSubstitution.lean, MultivariatePolynomials/BlockSubstitutionLaws.lean and IteratedBlockSubstitution.lean. I also checked Mathlib's bind₁/eval₂Hom_bind₁/eval_rename_prod_mk. The file has no simp attributes at all. I found two interface gaps: eval_blockSubst is not simp, and blockSubst has no unfolding equation. The first would send simp's evaluation of blockSubst to the already-simp-normal nested `eval` form with no cycle. For the second I would prefer a rfl equation lemma, not `@[simp]` on the unfolding, to avoid unwanted expansion. I did not run Lean, so I make no claim about simp behaviour; the changes are suggestions.

findings.excerpt: eval x (blockSubst p q) = eval (fun i => eval (fun j => x (i, j)) q) p
findings.problem: The main evaluation law for the opaque-looking definition `blockSubst` is not tagged `@[simp]`, so `simp` cannot see through `eval x (blockSubst p q)` unless a client unfolds the definition. Clients therefore invoke it by hand: `rw [eval_blockSubst]` followed by `simp` in `twoBlocks`, `simp only [eval_blockSubst]` in `twoStages`, and `simpa only [eval_blockSubst, eval_X, eval_C]` in `constantBlockNotIff`. The lemma is an oriented rewrite. The RHS is a plain `eval` of `p` at a function and contains no `blockSubst`, so the rewrite terminates. In this file the proof of `eval_blockSubst_eq_zero_iff` also rewrites by hand and builds `hinner` manually, work a simp set could do.
findings.proposed_change: Mark the lemma `@[simp]`, i.e. `@[simp] theorem eval_blockSubst ...`. The statement is already in the canonical direction (eliminate `blockSubst` under `eval`). Then `twoBlocks` and `twoStages` should reduce to a bare `simp`, and the `rw [eval_blockSubst]` calls in the clients become unnecessary.
findings.benefit: Evaluation of block substitutions normalises automatically to nested `eval`s of `p` and `q`. This also composes with Mathlib's `eval_X`/`eval_add`/`eval_C` simp lemmas, so client proofs shrink and nested substitutions (`blockSubst (blockSubst p q) r`) normalise without bespoke `simp only` calls.

findings.excerpt: bind₁ (fun i => rename (Prod.mk i) q) p
findings.problem: No unfolding or equation lemma (e.g. `blockSubst_def`, or `coe`-style `aeval`/`bind₁` form) is provided, and the definition is not reducible for `simp`. Every consumer must either unfold it with `simp [blockSubst]`, which expands `blockSubst` into raw `bind₁`/`rename` terms, or use `change`. The file does this in `eval_blockSubst` (`change eval₂Hom (RingHom.id R) x (bind₁ ...`). Clients do it too: `homogeneousDegree` uses `change (aeval (fun i => rename (Prod.mk i) q) p).IsHomogeneous`, and the laws file uses `simp only [blockSubst, ...]` throughout. There are also no basic simp lemmas for the degenerate cases that the tests re-derive, such as `blockSubst (X i) q`, `blockSubst 0 q`, `blockSubst (C r) q` and `blockSubst (p + p') q`.
findings.proposed_change: Add a non-simp equation `theorem blockSubst_def (p q) : blockSubst p q = bind₁ (fun i => rename (Prod.mk i) q) p := rfl`. Add simp lemmas for the canonical constructors that keep `blockSubst` on the LHS: `blockSubst_X : blockSubst (X i) q = rename (Prod.mk i) q`, `blockSubst_zero`, `blockSubst_add`, `blockSubst_C`, and probably `blockSubst_mul`. Their RHS is smaller than the LHS, so there is no cycle. Keep the definition itself out of the default simp set, and use `blockSubst_def` explicitly in the few proofs that need the `bind₁` form.
findings.benefit: Callers can unfold in a controlled way and avoid `change` with an expression that duplicates the definition body. `simp` can then compute `blockSubst` on explicit polynomials, such as the test `blockSubst (X 0 + X 1) q = rename .. q + rename .. q`, through the structural lemmas. Today that test needs `simp [blockSubst]`, which exposes the internal `bind₁` encoding.

evidence.excerpt: change (aeval (fun i => rename (Prod.mk i) q) p).IsHomogeneous (e * d)
